U.S. oil producers narrow focus to low-cost Permian

U.S. crude oil production slipped slightly in May from the record set a month earlier as a temporary ceasefire with Iran took some of the heat out of prices and curbed the incentive to maximise short term output. 

Total crude and condensates output retreated to an average of 13.7 million barrels per day (b/d) from a record 14.0 million b/d in April, according to the latest data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration. 

Declines were led by lower output from federal waters in the Gulf of Mexico (1.9 million b/d) which dipped from a record high the month before (2.1 million b/d).  

But onshore output from the Lower 48 states (11.4 million b/d), mostly from shale plays, also edged down slightly after sharply accelerating the previous month. 

Within the Lower 48, production has become increasingly concentrated in just two states, Texas and New Mexico, which have the lowest drilling costs and most promising well sites ...
